_purpose: Single source of truth for: what each dataset IS (real/synthetic/calibrated), its vintage, and where the best real/updated version comes from. Resolves the 'which vintage, is it synthetic, where to get better' questions in one place.

nature_legend.REAL_CAPRI: Extracted from CAPRI GAMS/GDX or COCO — CAPRI's own numbers
nature_legend.REALITY_CALIBRATED: Standard coefficients tuned to match observed reality (not CAPRI's own)
nature_legend.SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK: Generated with structure+noise because no real file present — REPLACE
nature_legend.MIXED_BY_COLUMN: Nature varies by column - see column_nature. A file-level label hid synthetic columns inside a REAL_CAPRI file; record per column.

base_areas.csv.note: Median deviation from CAPRI LEVL was 69.3%. Staples were close (soft wheat 85.5 vs 91.2) but specialty crops were placeholders - tomatoes 1.61 where CAPRI has 0.01.

yields.csv.source: capreg DATA2 (res_17<MS>.gdx), regional, base year 2017, for 21 crop activities over 144 regions; COCO export elsewhere; synthetic remainder
yields.csv.validation_status: VALIDATED. Model error against the independent COCO2 2017 benchmark fell from 16.0% to 7.3% median over 285 country x activity pairs, with 85% now within 20% (was 61%). Source itself scores 4.8%; the residual gap is the 67 regions capreg does not reach.
yields.csv.note: Crop units are kg/ha, verified against German SWHE 7612.6 and BARL 6648.2. Dairy yield is NOT in YILD - capreg DCOW YILD is 2535 nationally, while the real milk yield is in COMI at 8384.4 kg/head. Taking YILD uniformly would have put dairy 3x too low. | Sprint 9s: crop columns rebuilt for all 248 regions from the 27 member-state dumps (tools/build/build_crop_economics_2017.py): area-weighted over the CAPRI activities of each crop (OLIV+TABO, OFAR+ROOF, TEXT for COTT/OFIB, SETA+FALL, TWIN for WINE); a crop the region does not grow takes its member state's values.
yields.csv.best_update: 2) GRAS definition - capreg 410.9 vs COCO2 17770 for the same country and year; 3) DCOW/BULL/PIGF merge, real but with no independent benchmark; 4) the 8 renamed livestock activities (SCOW/HENS/POUF/SOWS/CAFF/HEIF/SHGF); 5) the 104 regions capreg does not reach
yields.csv.crosswalk_coverage: 227 of 248 model regions resolved via the full Eurostat chain 1995->1999->2003->2006->2010->2013->2016->2021->2024->2027; 181 reached in the capreg data
yields.csv.OANI_resolution: CLOSED - not obtainable, and not a units problem. In CAPRI, OANI is a share-index pseudo-activity rather than a herd: LEVL is exactly 1.0 nationally and the regional LEVLs sum to 1.0 across NUTS-1 (verified DE, FR, IT, PL), so LEVL is a regional share of the national other-animals residual. YILD (932709 for DE) is simply the value that satisfies PROD = LEVL * YILD / 1000. No per-head yield exists to import. The x1000 rescaling at cons_levls.gms:877 is internal, symmetric, reversed at line 2617, and does not describe the delivered data. OANI should stay on a literature-anchored placeholder, labelled as structurally unavailable rather than pending extraction.

producer_prices.csv.source: capreg DATA2 MPRI (EUR/t), regional, GDX read; national series as fallback
producer_prices.csv.note: The national series was materially wrong for specialty crops: other vegetables 30.8 EUR/t against CAPRI 495.9, tobacco 43.8 against 2574.7, other fruit 24.4 against 1295.7. Median deviation across 28 comparable activities was 37.5%. This was the cause of the long-standing validator warning about implausible specialty-crop losses, which fell from 418 cells to 105 once regional prices and CAPRI costs were used together. Prices and costs must be merged as a pair: CAPRI costs with the old prices leaves staples at a loss, because the old pair was internally consistent only with itself. | Sprint 9s: crop columns rebuilt for all 248 regions from the 27 member-state dumps (tools/build/build_crop_economics_2017.py): area-weighted over the CAPRI activities of each crop (OLIV+TABO, OFAR+ROOF, TEXT for COTT/OFIB, SETA+FALL, TWIN for WINE); a crop the region does not grow takes its member state's values.
producer_prices.csv.best_update: the residual 105 warnings are all in the 56 regions capreg does not cover

world_prices.csv.source: CAPRI SUA, with EGGS replaced from capmod res_0_1717
world_prices.csv.note:
Validated independently for the first time. EU producer prices (DATA2 MPRI, a verified GDX read) do not touch this file, so the producer/world ratio is a genuine external check: a domestic price far below the world price cannot hold, because producers would export instead.

Result: for SWHE, OCER, POTA, PULS, OVEG, APPL and CITR the MODEL is the more plausible source. CAPRI's world prices for those sit 25-60% ABOVE the EU farm-gate price for commodities the EU imports heavily (citrus 56% extra-EU, other fruit 56%, pulses 37%), which arbitrage does not permit. This overturns the earlier suspicion that the round-number values were placeholders CAPRI would correct - they look like placeholders but they are closer to right.

EGGS is the exception and was decisive the other way: the model carried 63.4 EUR/t, which is 0.063 EUR/kg and not a price eggs have ever traded at. The EU farm-gate egg price from MPRI HENS is 1193.1 EUR/t against CAPRI's world price of 1173.8, a ratio of 1.02. EGGS has been corrected to 1173.8; the market module still clears 12/12.
world_prices.csv.best_update: OLIV (ratio 0.39) and SHGM (0.32) have model world prices well ABOVE the EU producer price with no CAPRI value to compare - these are now the least defensible entries in the file. CHES, SKIM and BUTR cannot be checked this way at all: they are processed products and MPRI carries only farm-gate activities.
world_prices.csv.builder: tools/build/build_world_prices.py (29 October 2026): every row from CAPRI's FAO_agg world prices (OLIV, FPRI derived from CAPRI's data); the evaluation above describes the file as it was before

variable_costs.csv.source: capreg DATA2 TOIN (total intermediate input, EUR/ha), GDX read
variable_costs.csv.coverage: 4627 cells replaced across 192 regions; 56 regions keep prior values
variable_costs.csv.note: Previously labelled REAL_CAPRI with source "CAPRI" but sourced through the Excel path. Median deviation from CAPRI TOIN was 54.8%, with OVEG at 207% and identical values filled across OVEG and TOMA in the same region, indicating group-level fill rather than per-activity data. Note that TOIN is total intermediate input, which is a slightly broader concept than "variable cost"; the two are treated as equivalent here because CAPRI computes gross value added as output minus TOIN, which is the margin the supply module needs. | Sprint 9s: crop columns rebuilt for all 248 regions from the 27 member-state dumps (tools/build/build_crop_economics_2017.py): area-weighted over the CAPRI activities of each crop (OLIV+TABO, OFAR+ROOF, TEXT for COTT/OFIB, SETA+FALL, TWIN for WINE); a crop the region does not grow takes its member state's values.
variable_costs.csv.best_update: cover the 56 regions capreg does not reach

Now BPS = CAPRI's premiums per ha of UAA (UAAR PRME); ANC, AES, ORGANIC, COUPLED = 0 (CAPRI's results carry no split by instrument). supply_elasticities_regional.csv.coverage: 173 model regions x 15 crops, up from 107 regions
supply_elasticities_regional.csv.note: The previous file reproduced the same PELA 2005 slice but was CLIPPED at 4.5 rather than dampened: 270 cells sat at exactly 4.500. CAPRI's rule is min(8, sqrt(e) + 4.5 - sqrt(4.5)), so the affected cells averaged 4.50 where CAPRI gives 5.27, and the largest (DEB2/OATS, raw 111.0) was understated by 44%. This is the same truncation error that was in the code, baked into the data as well.

capmod_world_prices_2017.csv.source: capmod res_0_1717 dataOut Fob at exporter=World, import-weighted
capmod_world_prices_2017.csv.note: Fob is dimensioned by IMPORTER, because it is the free-on-board price that importer faces on its own bundle: barley is 281.0 for Norway and 132.5 for the UK in the same year. A single reference price therefore has to be constructed, and the import-weighted mean is used here. Validation against the base-fidelity reference values is mixed: BEEF, POUM and BUTT agree within 2%, MILK 5%, BARL 9%, MAIZ 16%, PORK 18%, WHEA 26% - but SOYA is 46% out and CHES 115%. NOT merged: the base-fidelity test compares the model's solved prices AGAINST this file, so a wrong value would be confirmed rather than caught. The outliers need explaining first.

capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.coverage: 73528 rows, 80 trade regions (34 real NUTS-national), 45 products
capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.note: The livestock supply elasticities that were the single largest verification gap. Own-price EU medians: BEEF 0.72, PORK 0.69, MILK 0.55, EGGS 0.76, POUM 0.75, SGMT 0.82. IMPORTANT it is MARKET level: regions are COUNTRY codes (XX000000) not NUTS-2, and products are market commodities (MILK, BEEF) not supply activities (DCOW, BULL). So it feeds the MARKET module's supply response, not the regional PMP calibration. The Excel export of the same file (elas1717defaulta_export.xlsx) returned a ZERO own-price diagonal; the direct GDX read gives the correct 2635-row diagonal, a clean demonstration of why the Excel path was abandoned.
capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.best_update: wire the EU medians into the market module supply response; regional PMP livestock elasticities remain unavailable (pmppar has no livestock terms)

pmp_quad_techn.csv.coverage: 56 activities incl. 18 livestock, ~270 regions each, 9494 rows
pmp_quad_techn.csv.note: CORRECTION to a prior error. The ingest regex required the tag pattern T1.T1, which crops use, but livestock activities use T.T. Every livestock PMP term was therefore silently dropped, and this was repeatedly and wrongly reported as 'CAPRI has no regional livestock elasticities'. CAPRI does: BULL, PIGF, SOWS, HENS, SCOW, DCOL and 12 others each carry a regional quadratic PMP term in ~270 regions. The regex now accepts both tags. Same class of error as the MAIZ/CORN bug: a filter that silently discards rather than flags.
pmp_quad_techn.csv.best_update: The livestock PMP terms are captured but not yet turned into elasticities: the derivation needs revenue = yield x price x herd-level, and livestock lives in the herds/animal_numbers frames rather than the crop yields/areas frames the derivation reads. Extending the derivation to pull livestock revenue from HERD x MPRI would give regional livestock supply elasticities directly, complementing the market-level p_elasSupp already extracted.

pig_split_and_product_values.source: Eurostat pig census (total pigs, breeding sows) for heads; CAPRI 2017 regional results res_17* (SOWS, PIGF: LEVL, MREV, TOIN, TOOU, MANN, FCER/FPRO/FENE, YPIG, IPIG, final-product quantities) and national UVAG
pig_split_and_product_values.builder: tools/build/build_livestock_output_coef.py (the per-head tables, since 29 October 2026), tools/build/build_livestock_products.py and the other regular builders; until then tools/build/build_shg_split.py --reproduce (calls build_livestock_output_coef.build / build_product_values_by_market and the dependent builders)
pig_split_and_product_values.method: Sprint 5 (docs/COUPLING_SPRINTS.md). CAPRI's two pig activities replace the single PIGS: PIGS keeps the sows (census breeding sows), PIGF = total pigs - sows. Coefficients per model head as for every animal. Product values: CAPRI final-product quantity (COMI, BEEF, PORK, POUM, EGGS, SGMT) x national UVAG x LEVL / model heads, by market (columns ACT.MARKET); a market price change moves an animal's revenue by quantity x price change, product by product.
pig_split_and_product_values.why_not_MREV: CAPRI's MREV differs by activity: for SOWS it is piglet sales (DE94: 24.0 x 25.43 = 610.9 = MREV), for raised calves CAMR/CAFR and replacement heifers HEIR it is young-animal sales (DEA2: CAMR MREV 623.7 = UVAG YBUL; HEIR 1071.4 = UVAG YCOW), for suckler cows a quarter of their beef value. Moving MREV with the meat price double-counted young animals (also priced by the young-animal markets) for sows, calves and heifers and under-moved suckler cows 2.9x.
pig_split_and_product_values.not_covered: sheep and goat milk (SGMI, 42% of the median SHGP product value) has no market in the model, so its value does not move with any price
pig_split_and_product_values.result: F2F 2030 gap 6.75 -> 7.02 (split alone) -> 6.91 (with product values); beef animals -14.5% (CAPRI -18), beef production -14.4% (-14); sows and fatteners fall together (-29%) because nitrogen prices in the pig regions exceed the fattener margin, so the piglet market does not relocate fattening

histosol.source: p_OrgSoilOri (orgsoil_share.gdx), p_emifacOrganicSoil_ori (IPCC_wetlands_supplement_2013.gdx), FAO land use 2000 by climate zone (fao_landuse_2000.gdx, P) - project lead's gdxdumps in sources/envind/; FAO country codes from global/fao_codes_new.gms; fallowing calibration from capri_costsavings_2030.csv (FALLOW IHISCR/IHISGR) and 2030 CROP/GRAS levels
histosol.used_by: EnvironmentalModule (N2O_HIS in the GHG total), RegionalSupplyModel._histosol_columns (fallowing)
histosol.registered_fallback: climate-zone shares by member state (CAPRI maps FAO countries to member states); histosol base area fixed at base for the fallowing curvature; fallowing calibrated to the model's own land-row duals
histosol.finding: EU N2OHIS 13.2 Mt CO2-eq; fallowing ~0 in Farm-to-Fork (JRC121368 Table 17: 2% -> 9%): the model's land-row duals at base are a few EUR/ha (DE94 crop 4.5) against CAPRI's ~100 EUR/ha (costsaving0), so the rent fall that drives CAPRI's adoption is absent

manure_n2o.source: CAPRI 2017 res_17 (MANN, N2OMAN, N2OAPP, N2OGRA, N2OLEA per activity); technology effects ammonia_technology_effects.csv (N2OHOU, N2OAPP) and p_litRevAmmoTechsAdd.csv (ManAcid)

manure_n2o.registered_fallback: CAPRI's N2OHOU effect applied to housing and storage together (N2OMAN); combined air purification + cover options take their cover's effect; inhibitors on manure without the NMAN term; flat 2% of manure N where a region-animal has no CAPRI factors

capri_ref_2030_trajectory.note: Sprint 9p: CAPRI star 3.0 2030 Green Deal reference with endogenous technologies (res_2_1730greendeal_refpol_endotech_all_ini, LEVL and YILD per region) over CAPRI's 2017 results (res_17<MS>.txt); levels, yields and land types (ARAC, FRUN, GRAS, FALL) as regional factors; sheep and goats (SHGM+SHGF) and calves (CAMF+CAFF+CAMR+CAFR) as totals. The 2030 baseline's trajectory by default (tools/run/run_f2f_2030.py --trajectory).

trade_region_tariffs_capri.note: Sprint 9r: total ad-valorem equivalent of each trade region's protection on imports from outside it, 100 x (sum ImportQ x ImportP / sum ImportQ x (Fob + TCost) - 1) over CAPRI's bilateral flows (market_base_1717), the EU row's own formula (kept from eu_tariff_provenance.json; recomputed from the member states it agrees to 0.1 point). Replaces the loader's random non-EU tariffs (drawn from a module-level generator, so each model built in a process differed). Commodities without imports or without a CAPRI market: 0.

crop_premium_capri_9s.note: CAPRI PRME per model crop and region, all 248 regions, area-weighted over the crop's CAPRI activities. Replaces the 192-region capreg_cap_premium.csv for crops (its CAPRI codes OFAR, TWIN, TEXT, SETA never matched the model's).

ghg_coefs_capri_9s.note: CAPRI's CH4MAN and CH4ENT per model head (CAPRI total LEVL x item over the region's activities / census herd; 2030 by CAPRI's reference factors, capri_ref_ration_2030.csv items ghg_CH4MAN/ghg_CH4ENT), CO2LIM per ha of every crop activity (UAAR) and the member state's urea share of mineral N (CO2UREA / NMIN / (44/28)). Replace IPCC Tier 1 flat factors (manure CH4 EU 2017: 1,072 kt flat against CAPRI's 1,396), 600 kg limestone per arable ha and 30% urea.

yield_price_elasticity_9s.note: CAPRI supply/yield_elas.gms p_yieldElas: cereals 0.3, oilseeds 0.2, potatoes 0.2, others 0 (was 0.15 for every crop, a literature value).

capri_tables_to_csv_9s.note: CAPRI values that were dictionaries in supply_module.py (INPO, FERT, plant-protection shares of input cost from the 27 dumps; EU feed use per cereal, CAPRI 2030 FEDM) moved to CSV (project rule).

model_parameters_9t.note: Sprint 9t: every constant of the model's economics and accounts, one row each, with unit, kind (capri, ipcc, jrc121368, legal, literature, model_setting) and source; read by capri_mod/params.py. Literature: organic yield gap fallback (the Mitscherlich curvature and N-intensity floor removed 27 October 2026 with the nitrate-limit option, K33). Model settings: outer-loop damping, Armington premium bounds, land-rent rule (land market off).

land_market_merge_9t.note: Sprint 9t: combined CAPRI regions' land-type matrices as (sum Q_c^-1)^-1 (the sum of the land owners' responses) instead of the area-weighted average; Ireland's NUTS-2016 regions from their shares of IE01/IE02 (build_capri_base.IRELAND).

capri_phosphate_balance.status: in use (environmental accounts, both supply forms)
capri_phosphate_balance.source: CAPRI Green Deal 2030 reference (res_2_1730greendeal_refdefaulta) and the same run with endogenous technologies at their initial shares (res_2_1730greendeal_refpol_endotech_all_inidefaulta), dataOut: regional P balance items (EXCRET MTRADE MINFER NETF CRESID EXPPRD RUNANI IMPORT SURTOT SURSOI, PHOF), UAAR LEVL, per elementary crop LEVL PRET PCRD, per elementary animal activity LEVL MANP MANN RUNANI (ini run)
capri_phosphate_balance.used_by: EnvironmentalModule.compute_phosphorus_balance (p_input, p_uptake, p_surplus, p_mineral_input, p_manure_excretion, p_manure_net_export, p_crop_residues, p_runoff, p_surplus_soil), capri_mod/environmental/p_balance.py, io_results.flatten_outputs env_EU_p_*
capri_phosphate_balance.method: CAPRI's reports/calc_nbalance.gms with FNUT = PHOF, in t P2O5. Mineral P2O5: the NLP form's purchases (fertilisation block); without the block (conic form) CAPRI's NUTNED_ for P summed over the crop groups with the block's data. Runoff: CAPRI's N runoff share RunTot from the loss cascade applied to manure P2O5.
capri_phosphate_balance.validation: Formula with CAPRI's own levels (ini run; DE11, NL22, PL22, DK): EXCRET, CRESID exact, EXPPRD within 0.01%, RUNANI via capri-mod's cascade within 1e-6, IMPORT/SURTOT/SURSOI exact. Accounts at the model's base data against CAPRI's 2030 reference, EU kg P2O5/ha: excretion 27.8/27.6, mineral 15.6/15.6, residues 24.0/24.1, removal 53.1/53.4, surplus 14.4/13.9, runoff 1.6/1.4 (ini 1.5); regional surplus per ha correlation 0.99 (213 NUTS-2). NLP solutions: NUTNED_ summed over the groups equals the purchases.

norway_market_region_k56.note: KNOWN_ISSUES K56 (21 October 2026): Norway is the model's 30th trade region NOR, as CAPRI's market region NO000000 (aggregation/defaultA.agg), mapped in tools/build/recalibrate_trade_2017.py REGION_MAP; every per-region market file was rebuilt with its builder, so ROW no longer holds Norway (ROW_old = ROW_new + NOR to the files' rounding). The EU's dairy block and balances hold the EU member states only; Norway's dairy block is a non-EU one (trade region NOR) with its raw milk from its supply models in the market. Side effects of the rebuild: armington_params.csv dairy eta (HCON-weighted over non-EU regions, now with Norway) moved by at most 3e-4; world_prices.csv FPRI 252.66 -> 252.74 EUR/t (export-weighted 2017 market prices: Norway's exports now count); trade_flows_2017.csv gains an all-zero SHGM column (the builder's commodity list).

norway_pigs.method: PIGS := CAPRI SOWS HERD, PIGF := CAPRI PIGF HERD, through tools/build/build_capri_base.build_spec (imported): NO02, NO06, NO07 their own CAPRI region; NO01, NO03, NO04, NO05 Eurostat cattle shares of NO08 + NO09 + NO0A.
